words.enDefinition: Learning that links events or connects actions with their consequences

examples.en: The lecture introduces associative learning with examples involving sounds and pictures on a screen.
examples.zh: 讲座用屏幕上的声音和图片示例来介绍「联结学习」。

examples.en: Our worksheet groups two kinds of conditioning under the heading associative learning.
examples.zh: 习题把两类条件作用归入「联结学习」这一标题下。

words.enDefinition: Experience-dependent change in responsiveness without learning an association between events

examples.en: The textbook uses a repeated sound to introduce nonassociative learning in the first paragraph.
examples.zh: 教材第一段用反复播放的声音来介绍「非联结学习」。

examples.en: We classified the declining response to a single tone as nonassociative learning.
examples.zh: 我们把对同一音调逐渐减弱的反应归为「非联结学习」。

words.enDefinition: Declining response to a repeated stimulus through a learning process

examples.en: In the simulation, habituation shows up as a weaker response to each identical tone.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，「习惯化」表现为对每次相同音调的反应越来越弱。

examples.en: The student asked whether the declining response reflected habituation or temporary fatigue.
examples.zh: 学生问，反应减弱究竟反映了「习惯化」还是短暂疲劳。

words.enDefinition: Return of a response to a habituated stimulus after a different stimulus

examples.en: The animation illustrates dishabituation when a new sound restores responding to the familiar tone.
examples.zh: 动画用新声音使对熟悉音调的反应恢复来说明「去习惯化」。

examples.en: We marked dishabituation at the point where the response to the original cue recovered.
examples.zh: 我们在对原先线索的反应恢复的位置标出了「去习惯化」。

words.enDefinition: Heightened responsiveness to stimulation following prior exposure to a stimulus

examples.en: The graph illustrates sensitization with a stronger response to the same gentle sound.
examples.zh: 图表用对同一轻柔声音更强的反应来说明「敏感化」。

examples.en: Our group contrasted sensitization with habituation using the two simulated response curves.
examples.zh: 我们组用两条模拟反应曲线对照了「敏感化」与习惯化。

words.enDefinition: Learning in which one stimulus comes to predict another stimulus

examples.en: The classical conditioning simulation links a colored square with a sound that follows it.
examples.zh: 「经典条件反射」模拟将一个彩色方块与随后出现的声音建立联系。

examples.en: We mapped each stimulus onto the classical conditioning diagram during the tutorial.
examples.zh: 辅导课上，我们把各个刺激对应到「经典条件反射」示意图。

words.enDefinition: Stimulus that initially does not elicit the response being studied

examples.en: The square begins as a neutral stimulus in the illustrated conditioning task.
examples.zh: 在图示的条件作用任务中，方块最初是「中性刺激」。

examples.en: We looked for a neutral stimulus before any learned response appeared in the animation.
examples.zh: 我们在动画出现任何习得反应之前寻找「中性刺激」。

words.enDefinition: Stimulus that elicits a particular response without prior associative learning

examples.en: In our simulated diagram, the unconditioned stimulus already elicits a response before training begins.
examples.zh: 在模拟示意图中，「无条件刺激」在训练开始前就能引发反应。

examples.en: The worksheet asks which event represents the unconditioned stimulus in this example.
examples.zh: 习题问，示例中的哪个事件是「无条件刺激」。

words.enDefinition: Reaction elicited by a stimulus without the need for learning

examples.en: The first panel shows the unconditioned response before the two events have ever occurred together.
examples.zh: 第一幅图显示，在两个事件首次同时出现之前就有「无条件反应」。

examples.en: We labeled the blink to the puff in the illustration as an unconditioned response.
examples.zh: 我们将图中气流引起的眨眼标为「无条件反应」。

words.enDefinition: Previously neutral cue that elicits a response after associative learning

examples.en: The familiar tone becomes a conditioned stimulus after consistently predicting the next event.
examples.zh: 熟悉的音调在能够持续预测后续事件之后成了「条件刺激」。

examples.en: We circled the conditioned stimulus that appeared alone in the final animation panel.
examples.zh: 我们圈出了动画最后一幅画面里单独出现的「条件刺激」。

words.enDefinition: Learned reaction elicited by a cue that predicts another stimulus

examples.en: The chart shows a conditioned response when the familiar cue appears by itself.
examples.zh: 图表显示，当熟悉的线索单独出现时会产生「条件反应」。

examples.en: We compared the conditioned response in the model with the response before learning.
examples.zh: 我们比较了模型里的「条件反应」和学习之前的反应。

words.enDefinition: Presentation of two stimuli in relation to one another during conditioning

examples.en: The first section of the animation illustrates stimulus pairing with two simple symbols.
examples.zh: 动画的第一部分用两个简单符号说明「刺激配对」。

examples.en: We labeled the stimulus pairing phase separately from the trials with one cue alone.
examples.zh: 我们将「刺激配对」阶段与只呈现一个线索的试次分开标注。

words.enDefinition: Initial development of a learned response during conditioning trials

examples.en: The rising part of the simulated curve represents conditioned response acquisition in the exercise.
examples.zh: 在练习中，模拟曲线的上升部分代表「条件反应习得」。

examples.en: We compared conditioned response acquisition across two sets of fictional trials with different cues.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两组采用不同线索的虚构试次中的「条件反应习得」。

words.enDefinition: Graph showing how a learned response develops across successive trials

examples.en: Our group drew an acquisition curve from the simulated responses in the early trials.
examples.zh: 我们组用早期试次中的模拟反应数据画出了一条「习得曲线」。

examples.en: The acquisition curve rises quickly and then levels off near the end of the graph.
examples.zh: 「习得曲线」先快速上升，到图表末端附近变得平缓。

words.enDefinition: Decline in a learned reaction when its cue no longer predicts another stimulus

examples.en: The diagram marks conditioned response extinction after the signal stops predicting the next sound.
examples.zh: 图表将「条件反应消退」标在信号无法继续预测下一个声音之后。

examples.en: Our results table puts conditioned response extinction below the separate rows for initial learning.
examples.zh: 结果表将「条件反应消退」放在单独列出的初步习得数据下方。

words.enDefinition: Trial in which the previously expected outcome is withheld after a cue

examples.en: During each extinction trial in the animation, the original cue appeared by itself.
examples.zh: 在动画的每次「消退试次」中，原先的线索都是单独出现的。

examples.en: We counted a brief response during the first extinction trial in the mock dataset.
examples.zh: 我们在模拟数据的第一次「消退试次」中记录到一次短暂反应。

words.enDefinition: Reappearance of an extinguished learned response after a period of rest

examples.en: The model shows spontaneous recovery when a weak learned response returns after a pause.
examples.zh: 模型用停顿后弱化的习得反应重新出现来说明「自发恢复」。

examples.en: We found spontaneous recovery after the break but before any new stimulus pairing.
examples.zh: 我们发现「自发恢复」发生在休息之后、任何新的刺激配对之前。

words.enDefinition: Return of an extinguished response when the context changes after extinction

examples.en: The simulated renewal effect appears when the screen returns to its original background color.
examples.zh: 屏幕回到起初的背景色时，出现了模拟的「更新效应」。

examples.en: We compared the renewal effect with recovery after a delay in the same setting.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「更新效应」与在同一情境下延迟后的恢复。

words.enDefinition: Transfer of a learned response to stimuli resembling the original cue

examples.en: The stimulus generalization exercise uses several shades of blue to represent similar cues.
examples.zh: 「刺激泛化」练习用深浅不同的蓝色代表相似线索。

examples.en: We saw stimulus generalization when similar sounds produced responses in the classroom simulation.
examples.zh: 在课堂模拟中，相似的声音也引起反应时，我们看到了「刺激泛化」。

words.enDefinition: Pattern relating response strength to similarity with a learned cue

examples.en: The generalization gradient peaks at the original shade and falls toward the other colors.
examples.zh: 「泛化梯度」在原来的色调处达到峰值，向其他颜色逐渐下降。

examples.en: Our team plotted the generalization gradient using the response scores from the simulation.
examples.zh: 我们组用模拟中的反应分数画出了「泛化梯度」。

words.enDefinition: Learned difference in responding to stimuli that signal different events

examples.en: The game illustrates stimulus discrimination by associating only one of two shapes with points.
examples.zh: 游戏只将两种图形中的一种与得分关联起来，以说明「刺激辨别」。

examples.en: We compared stimulus discrimination and generalization using the same simulated set of colors.
examples.zh: 我们用同一组模拟颜色比较了「刺激辨别」与泛化。

words.enDefinition: Learning in which an established conditioned cue supports conditioning of another cue

examples.en: The chart illustrates higher-order conditioning by adding a second cue after the first is learned.
examples.zh: 图表用学会第一个线索后加入第二个线索来说明「高阶条件作用」。

examples.en: Our lecturer distinguished higher-order conditioning from repeating the original pair of events.
examples.zh: 老师区分了「高阶条件作用」与反复呈现最初的一对事件。

words.enDefinition: Learning that a cue signals omission of an otherwise expected event

examples.en: The second cue in the model illustrates conditioned inhibition by signaling the missing sound.
examples.zh: 模型中的第二个线索通过预示声音不会出现来说明「条件性抑制」。

examples.en: The class looked for conditioned inhibition on trials where the expected event was absent.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们在预期事件未出现的试次中寻找「条件性抑制」的迹象。

words.enDefinition: Weak learning about a new cue alongside an already predictive cue

examples.en: The graph shows a blocking effect when the first color already predicts the sound.
examples.zh: 图表显示，当第一个颜色已经能预测声音时，会出现「阻断效应」。

examples.en: We discussed the blocking effect after comparing two simulated groups with different learning histories.
examples.zh: 我们比较了学习经历不同的两个模拟组，随后讨论了「阻断效应」。

words.enDefinition: Reduced learning about one cue presented alongside a more salient cue

examples.en: The simulation illustrates overshadowing when a bright color dominates a faint pattern.
examples.zh: 模拟用鲜亮的颜色比淡淡的图案更显眼的情形说明「遮蔽效应」。

examples.en: We compared overshadowing across cue pairs with very different levels of visibility.
examples.zh: 我们比较了明显程度相差很大的不同线索对之间的「遮蔽效应」。

words.enDefinition: Relationship indicating how much a cue predicts a particular outcome

examples.en: The worksheet compares predictive contingency for two symbols that appear before the same sound.
examples.zh: 习题比较了在同一声音之前出现的两个符号各自的「预测依存关系」。

examples.en: A short timeline alone does not tell us how strong predictive contingency is.
examples.zh: 一条简短时间线本身无法告诉我们「预测依存关系」有多强。

words.enDefinition: Occurrence of two events close together in time during learning

examples.en: The animation uses closely spaced flashes to illustrate temporal contiguity between two events.
examples.zh: 动画用间隔很短的闪光说明两个事件之间的「时间邻近性」。

examples.en: We discussed temporal contiguity without assuming that either simulated event predicted the other.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「时间邻近性」，没有预设任何一个模拟事件会预测另一个。

words.enDefinition: Learned avoidance of a flavor associated with subsequent discomfort

examples.en: The lecture presents conditioned taste aversion as a textbook example of selective associative learning.
examples.zh: 讲座将「条件性味觉厌恶」作为选择性联结学习的教材例子。

examples.en: We read a fictional vignette about conditioned taste aversion and identified the remembered flavor.
examples.zh: 我们阅读了一则有关「条件性味觉厌恶」的虚构短例，并辨认出当事人记住的味道。

words.enDefinition: Learning in which consequences change the future frequency of behavior

examples.en: The course introduces operant conditioning with a simple simulation of choices and points.
examples.zh: 课程用一个选择与得分的简单模拟来介绍「操作性条件作用」。

examples.en: Our group compared operant conditioning with learning that links two events on the screen.
examples.zh: 我们组比较了「操作性条件作用」和对屏幕上两个事件建立联结的学习。

words.enDefinition: Principle that satisfying consequences increase the likelihood of preceding behavior

examples.en: The lecture traces the law of effect to Thorndike's early work on learning.
examples.zh: 讲座追溯了「效果律」与桑代克早期学习研究的联系。

examples.en: We used a points game to illustrate the law of effect without running an experiment.
examples.zh: 我们用积分游戏说明了「效果律」，没有实际开展实验。

collocations: historical account of the law of effect

words.enDefinition: Behavior whose future occurrence is affected by the consequences it produces

examples.en: The simulation counts each press of the green button as an operant response.
examples.zh: 模拟把每次按绿色按钮都计为一次「操作性反应」。

examples.en: We graphed the operant response frequencies shown for the two levels of the game.
examples.zh: 我们把游戏两个关卡的「操作性反应」次数画成了图。

words.enDefinition: Event following a behavior that can modify its future occurrence

examples.en: A point on the screen serves as the response consequence in our simulation.
examples.zh: 在我们的模拟中，屏幕上增加一分就是「反应后果」。

examples.en: We identified the response consequence that followed a correct selection in the practice game.
examples.zh: 我们辨认出了练习游戏中正确选择之后出现的「反应后果」。

words.enDefinition: Increase in behavior because a stimulus is presented after that behavior

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates positive reinforcement with extra points and more frequent correct selections.
examples.zh: 习题用获得额外积分后正确选择增多的情形说明「正强化」。

examples.en: We discussed positive reinforcement after the simulated players repeated the rewarded move more often.
examples.zh: 模拟玩家更频繁地重复能得分的动作之后，我们讨论了「正强化」。

words.enDefinition: Increase in behavior because that behavior removes or prevents a stimulus

examples.en: The worksheet depicts negative reinforcement when silencing an alert makes a button press more frequent.
examples.zh: 习题用按键让提示音停止、此后按键更频繁的情形说明「负强化」。

examples.en: In the lecture, negative reinforcement was identified by an increase in the response rate.
examples.zh: 讲座以反应频率上升来识别「负强化」。

words.enDefinition: Decrease in behavior because a stimulus is presented after that behavior

examples.en: The simulated game illustrates positive punishment when an added warning reduces invalid moves.
examples.zh: 模拟游戏用增加提示后无效操作减少来说明「正惩罚」。

examples.en: We classified the added error signal as positive punishment only because the response decreased.
examples.zh: 我们之所以把新增错误提示归为「正惩罚」，是因为相关反应减少了。

words.enDefinition: Decrease in behavior because a stimulus is removed after that behavior

examples.en: In the simulation, negative punishment occurs when losing points reduces a particular move.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，扣分使某一动作减少，体现了「负惩罚」。

examples.en: The checklist identifies negative punishment using both the point loss and the declining response.
examples.zh: 核对表根据分数损失和反应减弱这两个现象识别「负惩罚」。

collocations: distinguish negative punishment from negative reinforcement

words.enDefinition: Consequence that increases future occurrence of the behavior it follows

examples.en: A game point counted as a reinforcer only when the response became more frequent.
examples.zh: 游戏积分只有在相关反应变得更频繁时才算「强化物」。

examples.en: The simulation compares how often a particular symbol serves as a reinforcer.
examples.zh: 模拟比较了一个特定符号作为「强化物」发挥作用的频率。

words.enDefinition: Consequence that gains reinforcing value through association with other reinforcers

examples.en: The token becomes a conditioned reinforcer after players learn what it can buy.
examples.zh: 玩家知道代币能兑换什么之后，它就成了「条件强化物」。

examples.en: Our worksheet describes how the star icon became a conditioned reinforcer.
examples.zh: 我们的习题描述了星形图标如何成为「条件强化物」。

words.enDefinition: Consequence with reinforcing value that does not require prior learning

examples.en: The textbook lists water as a primary reinforcer when the example describes thirst.
examples.zh: 教材在描述口渴的例子中把水列为「初级强化物」。

examples.en: We compared learned symbols with a primary reinforcer on the review chart.
examples.zh: 我们用复习图表比较了通过学习获得意义的符号与「初级强化物」。

collocations: biological basis of a primary reinforcer
distinguish a primary reinforcer from a conditioned reinforcer

words.enDefinition: Relationship specifying when a reinforcer depends on an observed behavior

examples.en: The reinforcement contingency in the demo links points to selections of the matching shape.
examples.zh: 演示中的「强化依存关系」将得分与选中匹配图形联系起来。

examples.en: We described the reinforcement contingency separately from how much each game point was worth.
examples.zh: 我们将「强化依存关系」与每个游戏积分的价值分开描述。

words.enDefinition: Rule specifying which responses or occasions are followed by reinforcement

examples.en: The two simulated games use the same points but a different reinforcement schedule.
examples.zh: 两个模拟游戏使用同样的积分，但「强化时程」不同。

examples.en: We labeled each reinforcement schedule according to whether it depended on responses or time.
examples.zh: 我们根据各个「强化时程」取决于反应次数还是时间来分类标注。

words.enDefinition: Reinforcement delivered after every occurrence of a specified response

examples.en: The diagram represents continuous reinforcement with a point after every correct match.
examples.zh: 图示用每次正确匹配后都得一分来表示「连续强化」。

examples.en: In the mock data, continuous reinforcement applies throughout the first block of trials.
examples.zh: 在模拟数据中，整组初始试次都采用「连续强化」。

words.enDefinition: Reinforcement provided following only some occurrences of a specified response

examples.en: The simulation depicts intermittent reinforcement by leaving some correct matches without a point.
examples.zh: 模拟用部分正确匹配不得分的情形说明「间歇强化」。

examples.en: We compared intermittent reinforcement with a game that rewarded every correct selection.
examples.zh: 我们把「间歇强化」与每次选对都得分的游戏作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Reinforcement schedule requiring a constant number of responses per reinforcer

examples.en: In the simulation, the fixed-ratio schedule requires the same number of matches each time.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，「固定比率时程」每次都要求相同的匹配次数。

examples.en: We identified the fixed-ratio schedule by counting responses between successive point deliveries.
examples.zh: 我们通过数两次得分之间的反应次数来识别「固定比率时程」。

words.enDefinition: Reinforcement schedule varying the response count needed around an average

examples.en: The simulated variable-ratio schedule awards points after different numbers of correct matches.
examples.zh: 模拟「可变比率时程」在正确匹配达到不同次数后发放积分。

examples.en: The example lists an average response count for the variable-ratio schedule used in class.
examples.zh: 示例列出了课堂演示的「可变比率时程」的平均反应次数。

collocations: compare a variable-ratio schedule with a fixed ratio

words.enDefinition: Schedule reinforcing the first response after a constant time interval

examples.en: The game simulation uses a fixed-interval schedule tied to a regular countdown.
examples.zh: 游戏模拟使用与规律倒计时相连的「固定时距时程」。

examples.en: The graph shows responses building near each interval's end under a fixed-interval schedule.
examples.zh: 图表显示，在「固定时距时程」下，反应在每个时段临近结束时增多。

words.enDefinition: Schedule reinforcing the first response after each varying time interval

examples.en: In the model, eligible responses occur after different waits under a variable-interval schedule.
examples.zh: 模型采用「可变时距时程」，符合得分条件的反应出现在不等长的等待之后。

examples.en: We identified the variable-interval schedule because the waiting time changed across simulated rounds.
examples.zh: 我们通过模拟各轮的等待时间不同辨认出「可变时距时程」。

words.enDefinition: Greater response persistence during extinction after intermittent than continuous reinforcement

examples.en: The hypothetical chart illustrates the partial reinforcement extinction effect after points stop appearing.
examples.zh: 假设图表说明了积分停止出现后的「部分强化消退效应」。

examples.en: We discussed the partial reinforcement extinction effect by comparing responding during two simulated extinction phases.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个模拟消退阶段的反应情况，由此讨论「部分强化消退效应」。

collocations: test the partial reinforcement extinction effect
demonstrate a partial reinforcement extinction effect
account for the partial reinforcement extinction effect

words.enDefinition: Cue indicating that a specified response is likely to be reinforced

examples.en: In the simulation, a green frame acts as a discriminative stimulus for correct matches.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，绿色边框是提示正确匹配可得分的「辨别性刺激」。

examples.en: We identified the discriminative stimulus separately from the points earned by the player.
examples.zh: 我们将「辨别性刺激」与玩家获得的积分分开辨认。

words.enDefinition: Decline in an operant behavior after its prior reinforcement stops

examples.en: In the animation, operant extinction begins when correct clicks stop producing points.
examples.zh: 在动画中，正确点击停止得分后开始出现「操作性消退」。

examples.en: We compared how rapidly operant extinction occurred across the two simulated games.
examples.zh: 我们比较了两个模拟游戏中「操作性消退」发生的速度。

words.enDefinition: Temporary rise in responding shortly after previously available reinforcement ends

examples.en: The chart depicts a brief extinction burst before the response rate starts falling.
examples.zh: 图表显示，在反应频率开始下降之前有一次短暂的「消退爆发」。

examples.en: The simulator registered an extinction burst when key presses briefly increased after it stopped awarding points.
examples.zh: 模拟器停止给分后，按键次数短暂增加，记录到一次「消退爆发」。

words.enDefinition: Developing a target behavior by reinforcing progressively closer versions of it

examples.en: The textbook uses shaping by successive approximations to explain a fictional sequence of closer matches.
examples.zh: 教材用「逐次逼近塑造」来解释一系列越来越接近目标的虚构匹配。

examples.en: We identified shaping by successive approximations on the simulation chart beside the changing criteria.
examples.zh: 我们在模拟图表不断变化的标准旁标出了「逐次逼近塑造」。

collocations: example of shaping by successive approximations
stages of shaping by successive approximations

words.enDefinition: Frequency of a behavior measured before the experimental condition changes

examples.en: Our lab exercise uses the opening round to estimate the baseline response rate.
examples.zh: 实验课练习用第一轮来估算「基线反应率」。

examples.en: The simulated baseline response rate appears as a reference line on the main graph.
examples.zh: 模拟的「基线反应率」以参考线的形式出现在主图上。

collocations: change from the baseline response rate

words.enDefinition: Brief period of little or no responding immediately following a reinforcer

examples.en: The graph shows a postreinforcement pause right after the point appears onscreen.
examples.zh: 图表显示，积分一出现在屏幕上就发生了「强化后停顿」。

examples.en: We located a postreinforcement pause before the simulated response rate picked up again.
examples.zh: 模拟反应率再次上升前，我们在图上找到了「强化后停顿」。

words.enDefinition: Graph plotting total accumulated responses over successive points in time

examples.en: The cumulative record stays flat when the simulated player makes no new responses.
examples.zh: 模拟玩家没有作出新反应时，「累积反应记录」保持水平。

examples.en: We read the steep part of the cumulative record as a period of rapid responding.
examples.zh: 我们把「累积反应记录」中较陡的一段解读为反应密集的时段。

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of behavior or knowledge through watching another person's actions

examples.en: The classroom exercise shows observational learning through a silent demonstration of paper folding.
examples.zh: 课堂练习通过无声的折纸演示说明「观察学习」。

examples.en: We used observational learning to explain why participants copied the unfamiliar hand movement.
examples.zh: 我们用「观察学习」解释参与者为何会模仿陌生的手部动作。

words.enDefinition: Demonstration of an action that observers can learn to perform

examples.en: The tutor uses behavioral modeling to show a different way of arranging the tiles.
examples.zh: 老师用「行为示范」展示了另一种摆放图块的方法。

examples.en: Our group compared written instructions with behavioral modeling in a simulated classroom exercise.
examples.zh: 我们组在课堂模拟练习中比较了书面说明与「行为示范」。

words.enDefinition: Increased tendency to imitate after observing a model receive reinforcement

examples.en: The animation illustrates vicarious reinforcement when viewers copy the player who earns points.
examples.zh: 动画用观众模仿得分玩家的情形说明「替代性强化」。

examples.en: We identified vicarious reinforcement even though the observers had received no points themselves.
examples.zh: 尽管观察者自己没有得到积分，我们仍辨认出了「替代性强化」。

words.enDefinition: Reduced tendency to imitate after observing negative consequences for a model

examples.en: The mock game illustrates vicarious punishment when observers avoid a move that cost someone points.
examples.zh: 模拟游戏用观察者避开曾让别人扣分的操作来说明「替代性惩罚」。

examples.en: The worksheet classifies the change as vicarious punishment because only the model lost points.
examples.zh: 习题把这一变化归为「替代性惩罚」，因为只有示范者被扣分。

collocations: distinguish vicarious punishment from direct punishment

words.enDefinition: Reproduction of an observed action by the person who watched it

examples.en: The task measures behavioral imitation by comparing each student's tile pattern with the demonstrated pattern.
examples.zh: 任务通过对照学生的图块排列与示范排列测量「行为模仿」。

examples.en: Our notes distinguish behavioral imitation from learning a rule described in writing.
examples.zh: 我们的笔记把「行为模仿」与学习书面描述的规则区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of knowledge that becomes apparent only in later performance

examples.en: The simulation depicts latent learning during maze exploration before any timed test.
examples.zh: 模拟展示了在限时测验前探索迷宫的过程中发生的「潜伏学习」。

examples.en: We discussed whether latent learning could explain the improvement shown on the later trial.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「潜伏学习」能否解释后面试次中表现的改善。

words.enDefinition: Mental representation of spatial relationships in a known or explored environment

examples.en: The classroom model uses a cognitive map to explain shortcuts in a virtual town.
examples.zh: 课堂模型用「认知地图」解释参与者为何能在虚拟小镇走捷径。

examples.en: Our tutor described a student's remembered campus layout as a cognitive map.
examples.zh: 老师将一名学生记忆中的校园布局称为「认知地图」。

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of information without an intention to learn that information

examples.en: Our reading exercise measured incidental learning for words that nobody expected to be tested on.
examples.zh: 阅读练习测量了参与者对那些未料到会考查的单词的「偶然学习」。

examples.en: We discussed incidental learning after recognizing pictures that appeared alongside the assigned reading.
examples.zh: 认出随指定读物出现的图片后，我们讨论了「偶然学习」。

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of information with a deliberate goal of remembering or mastering it

examples.en: The intentional learning group knew that a vocabulary quiz would follow the reading.
examples.zh: 「有意学习」组知道阅读之后会有一次词汇小测。

examples.en: Our worksheet labels the deliberate study condition as intentional learning in the comparison.
examples.zh: 在这项对比练习里，习题把刻意学习的条件标为「有意学习」。

collocations: compare intentional learning with incidental learning

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of patterns or rules without conscious awareness of that knowledge

examples.en: The implicit learning task tests whether people pick up patterns they cannot describe.
examples.zh: 「内隐学习」任务检验人们能否习得自己说不出的规律。

examples.en: Our seminar used a mock sequence game to discuss evidence for implicit learning.
examples.zh: 研讨课用模拟序列游戏讨论「内隐学习」的证据。

words.enDefinition: Acquisition of knowledge with conscious awareness of what is being learned

examples.en: In the explicit learning condition, participants could explain the pattern they were learning.
examples.zh: 在「外显学习」条件下，参与者能够解释自己正在学习的规律。

examples.en: The class contrasted explicit learning with learning regularities that participants could not report.
examples.zh: 课堂将「外显学习」与参与者无法说出的规律习得相对照。

words.enDefinition: Influence of earlier practice on performance in a different task

examples.en: The transfer of training exercise compares practice on one keyboard with performance on another.
examples.zh: 「训练迁移」练习比较了在一种键盘上练习与在另一种键盘上操作的表现。

examples.en: Our group studied transfer of training using two fictional tasks with different button layouts.
examples.zh: 我们组用按钮布局不同的两个虚构任务研究「训练迁移」。

words.enDefinition: Improvement on a new task attributable to prior practice or learning

examples.en: In the simulation, positive transfer occurs when earlier practice improves the new matching task.
examples.zh: 在模拟中，先前练习使新的配对任务表现更好，体现了「正迁移」。

examples.en: We looked for positive transfer by comparing scores with those of the untrained group.
examples.zh: 我们通过对照未接受练习的小组的分数，寻找「正迁移」的迹象。

words.enDefinition: Worse performance on a new task attributable to prior practice or learning

examples.en: The negative transfer example shows old button habits interfering with a new layout.
examples.zh: 「负迁移」的例子显示，原先的按键习惯妨碍了对新布局的使用。

examples.en: We identified negative transfer when the trained group initially made more selection errors.
examples.zh: 经过练习的小组起初出现更多选择错误，我们由此辨认出「负迁移」。

words.enDefinition: Process of transforming information into a representation usable by memory

examples.en: The worksheet compares memory encoding for pictures and for the names of pictured objects.
examples.zh: 习题比较了对图片的「记忆编码」和对图中物品名称的编码。

examples.en: Our seminar discussed memory encoding before looking at how the same information is retrieved.
examples.zh: 研讨课先讨论了「记忆编码」，再考察同样的信息如何被提取。

words.enDefinition: Retention of encoded information over a period of time

examples.en: The diagram places memory storage between the initial processing and the later test.
examples.zh: 示意图把「记忆储存」放在初始加工和后来的测验之间。

examples.en: We compared two models of memory storage using the same classroom memory example.
examples.zh: 我们用同一个课堂记忆示例比较了两种「记忆储存」模型。

words.enDefinition: Process of accessing information that has been retained in memory

examples.en: The study guide explains memory retrieval with an example about recalling a name.
examples.zh: 学习指南用想起姓名的例子说明「记忆提取」。

examples.en: We observed faster memory retrieval when the practice question included a familiar picture.
examples.zh: 练习题出现熟悉的图片时，我们观察到更快的「记忆提取」。

words.enDefinition: Processing information with little deliberate effort or conscious control

examples.en: The lecture uses a familiar word to illustrate automatic processing during everyday reading.
examples.zh: 讲座用一个熟悉的词说明日常阅读中的「自动加工」。

examples.en: We compared automatic processing of a known symbol with effortful study of a new one.
examples.zh: 我们比较了对熟悉符号的「自动加工」与对新符号的刻意学习。

collocations: distinguish automatic processing from effortful processing

words.enDefinition: Processing information through deliberate attention and active mental effort

examples.en: The worksheet describes effortful processing when students deliberately organize unfamiliar words by meaning.
examples.zh: 习题用学生有意识地按意义整理陌生词汇的情形说明「努力加工」。

examples.en: We used a new abbreviation to illustrate effortful processing during the memory tutorial.
examples.zh: 我们在记忆辅导课上用一个新缩写说明「努力加工」。

collocations: contrast effortful processing with automatic processing

words.enDefinition: Framework relating later memory to qualitative differences in how material is processed

examples.en: The levels of processing framework distinguishes looking at a word from considering its meaning.
examples.zh: 「加工层次」框架区分观察词的字形与思考词意。

examples.en: Our lab notes compare proposed levels of processing for a simulated word memory task.
examples.zh: 我们的实验笔记对比了模拟单词记忆任务中设定的「加工层次」。

words.enDefinition: Forming a memory representation based on the meaning of information

examples.en: The activity illustrates semantic encoding by asking students to sort words by meaning.
examples.zh: 活动让学生按意思给词汇分类，以此说明「语义编码」。

examples.en: We compared semantic encoding with a task that focused only on a word's sound.
examples.zh: 我们将「语义编码」与仅关注词语读音的任务作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Forming a memory representation based on how something sounds

examples.en: The acoustic encoding condition asks students whether pairs of written words rhyme.
examples.zh: 「声音编码」组需要判断成对出现的书面单词是否押韵。

examples.en: We discussed acoustic encoding after seeing more confusion between words that sounded alike.
examples.zh: 看到读音相近的词更容易混淆后，我们讨论了「声音编码」。

words.enDefinition: Rehearsal that links new information with its meaning or existing knowledge

examples.en: In the example, elaborative rehearsal links an unfamiliar term with a concept we already know.
examples.zh: 例子中的「精细复述」把陌生术语与我们已经了解的概念联系起来。

examples.en: Our study group used elaborative rehearsal by explaining how each idea fit the previous chapter.
examples.zh: 我们学习小组通过解释各个观点与上一章的联系来进行「精细复述」。

words.enDefinition: Simple repetition used to keep information temporarily available in memory

examples.en: The model illustrates maintenance rehearsal with a student quietly repeating a room number.
examples.zh: 模型用学生小声重复教室号码的情形说明「维持性复述」。

examples.en: We separated maintenance rehearsal from making meaningful links among the new vocabulary words.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「维持性复述」与在新词之间建立意义联系。

words.enDefinition: Grouping separate pieces of information into larger memorable units

examples.en: Our tutor illustrated memory chunking by grouping the digits into familiar year patterns.
examples.zh: 老师把数字按熟悉的年份样式分组，以此说明「记忆组块化」。

examples.en: The worksheet compares memory chunking for familiar letter patterns and for random letters.
examples.zh: 习题比较了熟悉字母组合和随机字母的「记忆组块化」。

words.enDefinition: Principle that cue effectiveness depends on how the memory was originally encoded

examples.en: The experiment on encoding specificity tests whether a cue from study helps during recall.
examples.zh: 「编码特异性」实验检验学习时的线索能否帮助回忆。

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates encoding specificity by changing the context of the studied words.
examples.zh: 习题通过更换学过的词所处的语境来说明「编码特异性」。

words.enDefinition: Brief persistence of sensory information after the original stimulation ends

examples.en: The class diagram places sensory memory just after the first visual or auditory input.
examples.zh: 课堂示意图把「感觉记忆」放在最初的视觉或听觉输入之后。

examples.en: We compared the visual and auditory forms of sensory memory in the lecture.
examples.zh: 我们在讲座中比较了「感觉记忆」的视觉形式和听觉形式。

words.enDefinition: Very brief retention of visual information after a display disappears

examples.en: The slide uses a brief letter display to illustrate iconic memory in class.
examples.zh: 课堂幻灯片用短暂显示的字母来说明「图像记忆」。

examples.en: We discussed how the delay in a simulated task affects measures of iconic memory.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了模拟任务中的延迟会如何影响对「图像记忆」的测量。

words.enDefinition: Brief retention of auditory information after a sound has ended

examples.en: The textbook illustrates echoic memory with the lingering impression of a short sound.
examples.zh: 教材用短暂声音结束后留下的印象来说明「回声记忆」。

examples.en: We discussed echoic memory while comparing simulated memory for sounds and flashed letters.
examples.zh: 我们在比较声音与闪现字母的模拟记忆表现时讨论了「回声记忆」。

words.enDefinition: Limited retention of information over a brief period of time

examples.en: In the demo, students use short-term memory to report a color sequence immediately.
examples.zh: 在演示中，学生用「短时记忆」立即说出颜色序列。

examples.en: The worksheet distinguishes short-term memory from remembering material learned in an earlier semester.
examples.zh: 习题把「短时记忆」和记得上学期学过的内容区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Storage of information that remains accessible beyond brief immediate retention

examples.en: The review sheet distinguishes facts and skills as examples of long-term memory.
examples.zh: 复习资料将事实和技能归为「长时记忆」的不同例子。

examples.en: Our tutor discussed long-term memory when we recalled diagrams from last semester's course.
examples.zh: 我们想起上学期课程里的示意图时，老师讲解了「长时记忆」。

words.enDefinition: Limited system for temporarily holding and manipulating information during current tasks

examples.en: The task uses working memory to keep two numbers available while adding them.
examples.zh: 这项任务需要用「工作记忆」在做加法时暂时记住两个数字。

examples.en: Our notes distinguish working memory from simply repeating a few letters in order.
examples.zh: 我们的笔记区分了「工作记忆」与单纯按顺序重复几个字母。

words.enDefinition: Working memory component that controls attention and coordinates other components

examples.en: The model assigns coordination between simultaneous tasks to the central executive in the diagram.
examples.zh: 示意图中的模型将同时处理多项任务的协调工作交给「中央执行系统」。

examples.en: Our lecturer discussed the central executive while comparing two tasks competing for attention.
examples.zh: 老师在比较两项争夺注意力的任务时讲解了「中央执行系统」。

words.enDefinition: Working memory component that temporarily maintains speech-based information through storage and rehearsal

examples.en: The diagram connects the phonological loop with holding a short list of spoken letters.
examples.zh: 示意图把「语音环路」与记住一小列口头报出的字母联系起来。

examples.en: We used the phonological loop model to discuss silently repeating a new word.
examples.zh: 我们用「语音环路」模型讨论在心里重复新单词的现象。

words.enDefinition: Component of the phonological loop that briefly holds speech-based representations

examples.en: The phonological store holds a brief record of sounds in the working memory model.
examples.zh: 在工作记忆模型里，「语音存储器」能短暂保留声音的记录。

examples.en: We labeled the phonological store separately from the mechanism for silently repeating speech.
examples.zh: 我们将「语音存储器」与在心里重复话语的机制分开标注。

words.enDefinition: Silent or overt repetition that refreshes verbal information in working memory

examples.en: The class described silently repeating a name as a form of articulatory rehearsal.
examples.zh: 课堂把在心里重复一个名字描述为「发音复述」的一种形式。

examples.en: The model pairs temporary verbal storage with articulatory rehearsal to maintain a list.
examples.zh: 模型将暂时储存言语信息与「发音复述」结合，以记住一份列表。

words.enDefinition: Working memory component for temporarily holding and manipulating visual or spatial information

examples.en: The model uses the visuospatial sketchpad to explain mentally tracking locations on a grid.
examples.zh: 模型用「视觉空间画板」解释人们如何在心中跟踪网格上的位置。

examples.en: Our class related the visuospatial sketchpad to holding a shape in mind while rotating it.
examples.zh: 课堂将「视觉空间画板」与在脑海中保留并旋转图形联系起来。

words.enDefinition: Working memory component proposed to integrate information into temporary unified representations

examples.en: The revised model uses the episodic buffer to link visual and verbal information.
examples.zh: 修订后的模型用「情景缓冲器」把视觉信息与言语信息联系起来。

examples.en: We discussed how the episodic buffer might combine a picture with its spoken description.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「情景缓冲器」如何把图片与口头描述整合起来。

words.enDefinition: Amount of information a person can actively maintain during processing

examples.en: The exercise compares estimates of working memory capacity from two short classroom tasks.
examples.zh: 练习对比了两项短时课堂任务估得的「工作记忆容量」。

examples.en: Our group discussed why working memory capacity estimates can depend on the task used.
examples.zh: 我们组讨论了为什么「工作记忆容量」的估计值可能取决于所用任务。

collocations: individual differences in working memory capacity

words.enDefinition: Length of a digit sequence a person can reproduce under specified instructions

examples.en: The instructor explains digit span using an increasingly long series of spoken numbers.
examples.zh: 老师用越来越长的一串口述数字来解释「数字广度」。

examples.en: We compared digit span scores for recalling digits forward and backward in the demo.
examples.zh: 我们比较了演示中按正序和倒序回忆数字的「数字广度」分数。

words.enDefinition: Working memory assessment combining temporary retention with an interleaved processing activity

examples.en: The complex span task alternates solving simple sums with remembering items for later recall.
examples.zh: 「复杂广度任务」交替进行简单加法和记住稍后要回忆的项目。

examples.en: Our tutorial compares a complex span task with a task requiring only immediate repetition.
examples.zh: 辅导课将「复杂广度任务」与只要求立即复述的任务作了比较。

collocations: scores on a complex span task

words.enDefinition: Conscious recollection or recognition of previously learned events or information

examples.en: The worksheet treats remembering a studied definition as an example of explicit memory.
examples.zh: 习题把想起学过的定义列为「外显记忆」的一个例子。

examples.en: Our seminar compared reports of explicit memory with changes in speed on a skill task.
examples.zh: 研讨课比较了「外显记忆」报告与技能任务中的速度变化。

words.enDefinition: Effects of previous experience on performance without conscious retrieval of that experience

examples.en: The model illustrates implicit memory when earlier exposure changes performance without deliberate remembering.
examples.zh: 模型用先前接触影响表现而没有刻意回忆的情形说明「内隐记忆」。

examples.en: We compared evidence for implicit memory with the participants' reports of remembered items.
examples.zh: 我们把「内隐记忆」的证据与参与者报告记得的项目作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Memory for personally experienced events situated in a particular time or place

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates episodic memory with recollection of a particular visit to campus.
examples.zh: 习题用回忆某次到访校园的经历来说明「情景记忆」。

examples.en: We distinguished episodic memory from knowing the campus address without recalling a visit.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「情景记忆」与知道校园地址却未回想起到访经历。

words.enDefinition: Long-term knowledge of facts, concepts, and meanings detached from particular episodes

examples.en: The diagram links semantic memory with knowing what a familiar academic term means.
examples.zh: 示意图将「语义记忆」与知道熟悉的学术术语的意思联系起来。

examples.en: The class contrasted semantic memory with remembering where a definition was first learned.
examples.zh: 课堂将「语义记忆」与记得最初在哪里学到某一定义相对照。

words.enDefinition: Long-term memory expressed through the performance of learned skills or procedures

examples.en: The chapter illustrates procedural memory with fluent typing after extensive practice on a keyboard.
examples.zh: 本章用在键盘上大量练习后能流畅打字的情形说明「程序性记忆」。

examples.en: Our tutor discusses procedural memory by contrasting descriptions of a skill with its performance.
examples.zh: 老师通过对照描述一项技能和实际施展该技能来讲解「程序性记忆」。

words.enDefinition: Memory for one's own experiences and personal knowledge about one's life

examples.en: The writing exercise draws on autobiographical memory for each student's first day at university.
examples.zh: 写作练习让每位学生用「自传体记忆」回想自己入学的第一天。

examples.en: We discussed autobiographical memory using examples of remembered life events and personal facts.
examples.zh: 我们用人生事件的回忆和个人经历事实的例子讨论了「自传体记忆」。

words.enDefinition: Change in processing an item following earlier exposure to the same item

examples.en: The simulation shows repetition priming when viewers identify a repeated shape's color more quickly.
examples.zh: 模拟中，观察者辨认重复图形的颜色更快，显示出「重复启动」。

examples.en: We tested for repetition priming by comparing naming times for repeated and new words.
examples.zh: 我们比较了说出重复单词和新单词的用时，以检验「重复启动」。

words.enDefinition: Change in processing a target after exposure to a related meaning

examples.en: The animation uses semantic priming to explain faster responses after a related word appears.
examples.zh: 动画用「语义启动」解释为何呈现相关单词后的反应更快。

examples.en: We tested for semantic priming in a fictional dataset containing related and unrelated word pairs.
examples.zh: 我们在包含相关和无关词对的虚构数据里检验是否存在「语义启动」。

words.enDefinition: Retrieval of previously presented items in their original presentation order

examples.en: The exercise uses serial recall to check whether students remember the original order.
examples.zh: 练习用「序列回忆」检查学生是否记得原先的顺序。

examples.en: We counted misplaced letters as order errors in the serial recall condition.
examples.zh: 在「序列回忆」条件下，我们把放错位置的字母计为顺序错误。

words.enDefinition: Retrieval attempted directly after presentation or study of the target material

examples.en: The instructor recorded immediate recall as soon as the study list disappeared.
examples.zh: 学习列表一消失，老师就记录了「即时回忆」的表现。

examples.en: We compared immediate recall with performance after completing another short classroom activity.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「即时回忆」与完成另一项简短课堂活动后的表现。

words.enDefinition: Retrieval attempted after a period has elapsed since learning or presentation

examples.en: The delayed recall task took place after students finished the unrelated activity.
examples.zh: 学生完成无关活动后进行了「延迟回忆」任务。

examples.en: Our group plotted delayed recall scores for words studied earlier in the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们组把练习中先前学过的单词的「延迟回忆」分数画成了图。

words.enDefinition: Retrieval of studied items without specific cues or a required order

examples.en: In the free recall task, students list remembered words in any order.
examples.zh: 在「自由回忆」任务中，学生可以按任意顺序写下记得的单词。

examples.en: We chose free recall because the exercise focused on remembering items without hints.
examples.zh: 因为练习关注没有提示时能想起哪些项目，我们选用了「自由回忆」。

words.enDefinition: Retrieval of learned information with the assistance of a specific prompt

examples.en: The cued recall test shows the first word from each studied pair.
examples.zh: 「线索回忆」测验会显示每个学过的词对中的第一个词。

examples.en: Our tutor compared cued recall scores across two different types of hints.
examples.zh: 老师比较了两种不同提示下的「线索回忆」分数。

words.enDefinition: Ability to identify an item as previously encountered or studied

examples.en: The class exercise tests recognition memory by mixing familiar pictures with new ones.
examples.zh: 课堂练习把熟悉图片和新图片混在一起，以测量「再认记忆」。

examples.en: We compared recognition memory with the ability to list the pictures from memory.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「再认记忆」与凭记忆列出图片的能力。

words.enDefinition: Hint that helps someone access information already stored in memory

examples.en: In the worksheet, the first letter serves as a retrieval cue for the word.
examples.zh: 在习题中，该单词的首字母充当它的「提取线索」。

examples.en: We tested whether a picture was an effective retrieval cue for a studied name.
examples.zh: 我们检验了图片能否作为所学姓名的有效「提取线索」。

words.enDefinition: Processes through which a newly formed memory becomes more stable over time

examples.en: The diagram depicts memory consolidation as a gradual change after the initial learning period.
examples.zh: 示意图将「记忆巩固」描绘为初次学习之后逐步发生的变化。

examples.en: We discussed memory consolidation when comparing memory measured at different times after study.
examples.zh: 我们比较了学习后不同时间测得的记忆表现，并讨论了「记忆巩固」。

words.enDefinition: Time separating initial learning from a later test of memory

examples.en: The review chart lists the retention interval for each hypothetical memory test.
examples.zh: 复习图表列出了每次假设记忆测验的「保持间隔」。

examples.en: Our group compared two scores obtained after the same retention interval in the simulation.
examples.zh: 我们组比较了模拟中相同「保持间隔」之后得到的两个分数。

words.enDefinition: Practice that requires actively bringing previously learned information to mind

examples.en: Our study group used retrieval practice by answering questions with the book closed.
examples.zh: 我们学习小组通过合上书回答问题来做「提取练习」。

examples.en: The article compares retrieval practice with rereading the same short explanation about memory.
examples.zh: 文章比较了「提取练习」与重读同一段关于记忆的简短说明。

words.enDefinition: Improved later retention from taking a memory test compared with restudying

examples.en: The graph illustrates the testing effect using later scores after initial testing or rereading.
examples.zh: 图表对照了先测试和先重读两组的后续分数，以此说明「测试效应」。

examples.en: We discussed the testing effect using delayed scores from a fictional vocabulary study.
examples.zh: 我们用虚构词汇研究的延迟测验分数讨论了「测试效应」。

words.enDefinition: Better later memory for study episodes separated in time than compressed together

examples.en: The sample data illustrate the spacing effect when the same study time is spread out.
examples.zh: 样本数据用同等学习时间分散安排的情形说明「间隔效应」。

examples.en: We compared two schedules before interpreting the spacing effect in the fictional results.
examples.zh: 我们先比较了两种时间安排，再解释虚构结果中的「间隔效应」。

words.enDefinition: Practice spread across multiple sessions with intervals between them

examples.en: The worksheet uses three separate review sessions as an example of distributed practice.
examples.zh: 习题用三次分开的复习来举例说明「分散练习」。

examples.en: Our group labeled the calendar with distributed practice before comparing the test scores.
examples.zh: 我们组先在日历上标出「分散练习」，再比较测验分数。

collocations: compare distributed practice with massed practice

words.enDefinition: Practice compressed into one session or repeated with little time between attempts

examples.en: The classroom example uses one uninterrupted session to illustrate massed practice for vocabulary.
examples.zh: 课堂示例用一次不中断的学习说明词汇的「集中练习」。

examples.en: We compared scores after massed practice with scores after the spaced study schedule.
examples.zh: 我们比较了「集中练习」后的分数与分散学习安排后的分数。

collocations: compare massed practice with spaced practice

words.enDefinition: Memory advantage for information learners produce themselves rather than simply read

examples.en: The worksheet illustrates the generation effect by comparing completed words with words already printed.
examples.zh: 习题比较自行补全的单词和已经印全的单词，以说明「生成效应」。

examples.en: We discussed the generation effect after examining recall for answers students generated themselves.
examples.zh: 我们考察学生自己得出的答案在回忆中的表现后，讨论了「生成效应」。

words.enDefinition: Memory advantage for words spoken aloud during study over silently read words

examples.en: The demo contrasts reading words aloud and silently to illustrate the production effect.
examples.zh: 演示对比朗读和默读单词，以说明「产出效应」。

examples.en: In the simulated study, the production effect appeared on the later recognition test.
examples.zh: 在模拟研究中，「产出效应」体现在后来的再认测验中。

words.enDefinition: Variation in memory performance with an item's position in a sequence

examples.en: The chart depicts the serial position effect by plotting recall against each item's list position.
examples.zh: 图表按各项目在列表中的位置绘制其回忆表现，以展示「系列位置效应」。

examples.en: Our seminar used a short word list to introduce the serial position effect.
examples.zh: 研讨课用一个简短词表来介绍「系列位置效应」。

collocations: tests of the serial position effect

words.enDefinition: Better recall for early list items than for items in the middle

examples.en: The class graph shows a primacy effect for the first words on the list.
examples.zh: 课堂图表显示，列表开头的单词出现了「首因效应」。

examples.en: We examined the primacy effect separately from the improvement for items near the end.
examples.zh: 我们将「首因效应」与靠近末尾项目的表现改善分开考察。

words.enDefinition: Better recall for late list items than for items in the middle

examples.en: The demonstration shows a recency effect when students recall the last items particularly well.
examples.zh: 演示中，学生对最后几个项目回忆得特别好，体现了「近因效应」。

examples.en: We compared the recency effect for immediate recall with recall after a distraction.
examples.zh: 我们比较了即时回忆和经历干扰后回忆中的「近因效应」。

words.enDefinition: Graph showing how retention of learned information changes as time passes

examples.en: Our group sketched a forgetting curve from the simulated recall scores across several days.
examples.zh: 我们组根据几天的模拟回忆分数画了一条「遗忘曲线」。

examples.en: The textbook compares the first steep drop with the flatter part of the forgetting curve.
examples.zh: 教材把「遗忘曲线」开头的陡降与之后较平缓的部分相比较。

words.enDefinition: Failure to form an adequate memory representation when encountering information

examples.en: The instructor used encoding failure to explain why an unnoticed detail was never remembered.
examples.zh: 老师用「编码失败」解释为什么一项没注意到的细节从来没有被记住。

examples.en: We considered encoding failure when students could describe the object but not its label.
examples.zh: 当学生能描述物品但想不起标签时，我们考虑了「编码失败」。

words.enDefinition: Inability to access stored information at the time it is needed

examples.en: The example illustrates retrieval failure when a familiar word comes back after prompting.
examples.zh: 示例用提示后想起熟悉单词的情形说明先前发生了「提取失败」。

examples.en: We distinguished retrieval failure from never forming a usable memory of the item.
examples.zh: 我们把「提取失败」与一开始就没有形成可用记忆区分开来。

words.enDefinition: Disruption of new learning or remembering by information acquired earlier

examples.en: The model illustrates proactive interference when yesterday's list disrupts recall of today's list.
examples.zh: 模型用昨天的列表妨碍回忆今天的列表来说明「前摄干扰」。

examples.en: We tested for proactive interference by comparing recall after studying similar or unrelated words.
examples.zh: 我们比较了学过相似词或无关词之后的回忆表现，以检验「前摄干扰」。

words.enDefinition: Disruption of memory for earlier information by new learning or experiences

examples.en: The simulation depicts retroactive interference when the second list disrupts recall of the first.
examples.zh: 模拟用第二份列表妨碍回忆第一份列表来说明「倒摄干扰」。

examples.en: Our worksheet uses two lists of made-up words to demonstrate retroactive interference.
examples.zh: 我们的习题用两份虚构词汇列表展示「倒摄干扰」。

words.enDefinition: Temporary inability to retrieve a familiar word despite feeling it is accessible

examples.en: The lecture illustrates the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon with a familiar title that temporarily escapes recall.
examples.zh: 讲座用暂时想不起一个熟悉标题的情形说明「舌尖现象」。

examples.en: We used the tip-of-the-tongue phenomenon to discuss why a word can feel almost accessible.
examples.zh: 我们用「舌尖现象」讨论为什么有时觉得一个词马上就能想起来。

words.enDefinition: Process of deciding where a remembered detail or impression came from

examples.en: The source monitoring exercise asks whether a fact came from reading or discussion.
examples.zh: 「来源监测」练习要求判断某条事实来自阅读还是讨论。

examples.en: We discussed source monitoring when participants confused two speakers in the fictional transcript.
examples.zh: 参与者混淆了虚构笔录中的两名说话者，我们借此讨论了「来源监测」。

words.enDefinition: Distortion of memory by misleading information encountered after an event

examples.en: The lecture illustrates the misinformation effect with an inaccurate account in a fictional study.
examples.zh: 讲座用一项虚构研究中的不准确描述来说明「错误信息效应」。

examples.en: We compared remembered details from two fictional groups to discuss the misinformation effect.
examples.zh: 我们对照了两个虚构小组记得的细节，以讨论「错误信息效应」。

words.enDefinition: Recollection of something that did not occur or occurred differently

examples.en: The worksheet counts recalling an unshown picture as a false memory in the task.
examples.zh: 习题将任务中回忆起一张从未呈现的图片计为一次「虚假记忆」。

examples.en: The seminar discusses how a false memory can feel convincing despite being inaccurate.
examples.zh: 研讨课讨论「虚假记忆」为何虽然不准确，却依然能让人确信。

words.enDefinition: Estimate of how well recently studied information will be remembered later

examples.en: After studying the pair, each student recorded a judgment of learning before taking the quiz.
examples.zh: 学习词对后，每位学生在参加小测前记录了一次「学习判断」。

examples.en: We compared each judgment of learning with actual later recall in the fictional dataset.
examples.zh: 我们用虚构数据对照了各项「学习判断」及随后实际的回忆表现。

collocations: accuracy of a judgment of learning

words.enDefinition: awareness of holding information even when you cannot recall it

examples.en: The exercise asks about a feeling of knowing after the participant cannot recall a word.
examples.zh: 参与者未能回忆起单词后，练习询问是否有「知晓感」。

examples.en: We compared ratings of feeling of knowing with recognition scores from the later test.
examples.zh: 我们把「知晓感」评分与随后测验中的再认分数作了比较。

words.enDefinition: Measurement of retention from reduced effort needed to relearn previously studied material

examples.en: The instructor illustrates the method of savings by comparing initial study time with relearning time.
examples.zh: 老师用首次学习时间与重新学习时间的对比来说明「节省法」。

examples.en: We used the method of savings to interpret the shorter relearning time in the sample data.
examples.zh: 我们用「节省法」解释样本数据中较短的重新学习时间。

collocations: measure retention with the method of savings
